claims.statement: Adrenal incidentaloma warrants a 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test even when overt cortisol-excess signs are absent; frailty with limited life expectancy is an exception.
claims.limitation: Single directly verified current guideline; benign morphology is not a hormone assay.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the exact topic clinic cases and outside-hospital record reviews; see each claim boundary.

claims.statement: A homogeneous adrenal mass with unenhanced CT attenuation at most 10 HU needs no additional adrenal imaging solely for malignancy surveillance under ESE 2023, irrespective of size.
claims.limitation: Requires truly unenhanced acquisition and homogeneity; not applicable to invasive, symptomatic or hormonally active disease.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the exact topic clinic cases and outside-hospital record reviews; see each claim boundary.

claims.statement: After abnormal dexamethasone suppression in an incidentaloma, confirm ACTH independence, consider test interference and repeat suppression testing before making a treatment decision.
claims.limitation: An isolated nonsuppression result does not establish the visible nodule as the causal source.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the exact topic clinic cases and outside-hospital record reviews; see each claim boundary.

claims.statement: An initially normal adrenal hormonal evaluation need not be repeated routinely, but new endocrine signs or worsening hypertension or diabetes warrant reassessment.
claims.limitation: One directly verified guideline; stable imaging does not exclude changing hormone secretion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the exact topic clinic cases and outside-hospital record reviews; see each claim boundary.

claims.statement: For a surveilled indeterminate adrenal lesion, growth exceeding 20% of maximal diameter together with at least 5 mm over 6-12 months supports surgical reassessment.
claims.limitation: Low-certainty guideline criterion; applies to indeterminate lesions, not a universal cancer diagnosis or automatic operation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the exact topic clinic cases and outside-hospital record reviews; see each claim boundary.

claims.statement: An adrenal biopsy requires management-changing histology, indeterminate imaging and exclusion of hormone excess, particularly pheochromocytoma.
